reports.score.subject: Canvas course
reports.score.notice.selectSubject: Choose a Canvas subject to compare grades.
reports.score.notice.selectSubjectAndGra: Choose a Canvas subject and grade to compare homerooms.
reports.score.notice.selectSection: Choose a Canvas class label to compare its subjects.

reports.score.method.assignment: For each student and course, earned points are divided by possible points for graded assignments in the selected groups, converted to a 10-point score and rounded to 0.1. Eligible course results are then averaged. Ungraded work is excluded.
reports.score.englishProgrammesHint: Choose ESL, ELA, or both. Clearing the selection includes both. This filter only affects English results.
reports.score.englishProgrammeScope: English results include only the selected ESL/ELA courses; other courses grouped under English are excluded.
reports.score.englishBothNotice: With both selected, a student taking ESL and ELA contributes two course results.
reports.score.method.current: Canvas current course score (0–100%) is grouped by subject. This is a live Canvas progress measure, not an official calculated GPA. Term-specific current scores may be unavailable.
reports.score.method.bands: A+/A/B/C/D counts use the displayed score bands. C+D share = (C + D) ÷ all scored records in the row.
reports.score.method.bandsTest: Each student–course result uses earned ÷ possible points from graded assignments in the selected groups, converted to a 10-point score and rounded to 0.1 before banding. C+D share = (C + D) ÷ scored course results in the row.
reports.score.method.histogram: Each student–course result uses earned ÷ possible points from graded assignments in the selected groups, converted to a 10-point score and rounded to 0.1. Each result is counted once; the first range is 0–<5, then 0.5-point ranges.
reports.score.method.ranking: Each course result uses earned ÷ possible points from graded assignments in the selected groups, converted to a 10-point score and rounded to 0.1. Course results are averaged for each student; the overall value summarizes only the displayed students.
reports.score.referenceDifference: This source uses the actual Canvas data available: earned ÷ possible points for graded assignments in the selected groups. Canvas drop rules or weighting may differ from the overall course score.
reports.score.currentScoreNotice: This report shows the current course score supplied by Canvas on its native 0–100 scale.
reports.score.bandLegend: Result bands (score rounded to 0.1 out of 10)

reports.classes.title: Classes needing support
reports.classes.longDescription: A consistent Red–Amber–Green review by grade or class, based on the share of students with current early-warning signals.
reports.classes.note: Green means no students currently flagged, Amber means up to 10%, and Red means more than 10%. This first version uses grade cohorts; class-level grouping can be added when the reporting dataset is available.
reports.classes.noMatches: No grade or class matches this search.
reports.classes.settings.title: How Red–Amber–Green is determined
reports.classes.settings.hint: Each grade or class is classified from the share of students needing support. You can adjust the display thresholds for this report.
reports.classes.settings.formula: Flagged rate = students needing support ÷ total students in the grade or class × 100.
reports.classes.settings.amberHint: Review signals with the responsible team.
reports.classes.settings.validation: Green must be at least 0%, and Amber must be higher than Green and no more than 100%.
reports.classes.settings.summary: Current rule — Green: up to {green}; Amber: above {green} through {amber}; Red: above {amber}. Select “How grouping works” to see the formula or adjust thresholds.
reports.classes.settings.rowExplanation: {count}/{total} students need support ({rate}), so this group is {status}. Current thresholds: Green ≤ {green}, Amber ≤ {amber}, Red > {amber}.

reports.meals.ordered-no-ticket.title: Ordered meals without a ticket
reports.meals.ordered-no-ticket.descript: Students marked as having ordered a meal but not collected a meal ticket.
reports.meals.ordered-not-eaten.title: Ordered meals not eaten
reports.meals.ordered-not-eaten.descript: Students who ordered a meal in advance but did not print a ticket on the meal date, using the school's definition.
reports.meals.no-order.title: Students without a meal order
reports.meals.no-order.description: Students marked as not having ordered a meal in the ERP export.
reports.meals.coffee-frequency.title: Top Coffee Shop purchases
reports.meals.coffee-frequency.descripti: Rank students by total item quantity purchased at the Coffee Shop; view totals per student, day, week, or month.
reports.meals.ordered-not-eaten.logicHin: Ordered + no printed/collected ticket = not eaten. Count once per student/day/meal, using the same figures as the no-ticket report.
reports.meals.coffee-frequency.logicHint: Sum all item quantities per student by day, week, or month; rank highest to lowest within the selected period. Weeks run Monday to Sunday.
reports.meals.notEatenDefinition: The school counts an ordered meal without a printed/collected ticket as not eaten. This uses the same data as the ordered-without-ticket report, counted once per student, date, and meal.
reports.meals.coffeeNote: Total item quantity per student at the school's single Coffee Shop, combining every item in the ERP purchase feed. Weeks run Monday to Sunday.
reports.meals.statusNote: Meals are counted once per student, day, and meal from the corresponding ERP status export. The exports cover only the dates and students supplied by the ERP.
reports.meals.invalidDates: Choose a valid date or date range.
reports.meals.ordered-no-ticket.countLab: Meal orders without a collected ticket
reports.meals.ordered-no-ticket.countMea: One count = one student on one date for one meal with an order but no collected ticket. Breakfast and lunch count separately.
reports.meals.ordered-not-eaten.countMea: An advance order without a printed/collected ticket on the meal date counts as not eaten. Breakfast and lunch count separately.
reports.meals.no-order.countMeaning: One count = one student on one date for one meal marked not ordered by the ERP. Breakfast and lunch count separately.
reports.meals.coffee-frequency.countMean: Sum the quantity of every item purchased by the student, regardless of product type.
